On this page

> For AI agents: see [llms.txt](https://docs.convex.dev/llms.txt) for the complete documentation index. Markdown versions are available by adding .md to a page URL or requesting Accept: text/markdown.

Log streams enable streaming of events such as function executions and
`console.log`s from your Convex deployment to supported destinations, such as
Axiom, Datadog, PostHog, or a custom webhook.

The most recent logs produced by your Convex deployment can be viewed in the
Dashboard [Logs page](https://docs.convex.dev/dashboard/deployments/logs), the
[Convex CLI](https://docs.convex.dev/cli/overview), or in the browser console, providing a quick
and easy way to view recent logs.

Log streaming to a third-party destination like Axiom, Datadog, or PostHog
enables storing historical logs, more powerful querying and data visualization,
and integrations with other tools (e.g. PagerDuty, Slack).

Log streams require a Convex Pro plan.

Log streamsrequire a Convex Pro plan. [Learn\\
more](https://convex.dev/pricing) about our plans or
[upgrade](https://dashboard.convex.dev/team/settings/billing).

## Configuring log streams [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#configuring-log-streams "Direct link to Configuring log streams")

We currently support the following log streams, with plans to support many more:

- [Axiom](https://www.axiom.co/)
- [Datadog](https://www.datadoghq.com/)
- [PostHog](https://posthog.com/)
- Webhook to a custom URL

See the instructions for
[configuring an integration](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/#configuring-an-integration).
The specific information needed for each log stream is covered below.

### Axiom [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#axiom "Direct link to Axiom")

Configuring an Axiom log stream requires specifying:

- The name of your
[Axiom dataset](https://axiom.co/docs/reference/settings#dataset)
- An Axiom [API key](https://axiom.co/docs/reference/settings#api-token)
- An optional list of attributes and their values to be included in all log
events send to Axiom. These will be sent via the `attributes` field in the
[Ingest API](https://axiom.co/docs/send-data/ingest#ingest-api).

When configuring a Convex dataset in Axiom, a dashboard will automatically be
created in Axiom. You can find it in the _Integrations_ section of the
_Dashboards_ tab. To customize the layout of the dashboard, you can
[fork it](https://axiom.co/docs/dashboards/create#fork-dashboards).

![A dashboard in Axiom](https://docs.convex.dev/assets/images/axiom_dashboard-a989f50d9d1fe5d65e33ecafb7facea1.png)

### Datadog [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#datadog "Direct link to Datadog")

Configuring a Datadog log stream requires specifying:

- The [site location](https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/site/) of your
Datadog deployment
- A Datadog
[API key](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/api-app-keys/#add-an-api-key-or-client-token)
- A comma-separated list of tags that will be passed using the
[`ddtags` field](https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/tagging/) in all
payloads sent to Datadog. This can be used to include any other metadata that
can be useful for querying or categorizing your Convex logs ingested by your
Datadog deployment.

### PostHog [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#posthog "Direct link to PostHog")

Configuring a PostHog log stream requires specifying:

- A PostHog [project token](https://us.posthog.com/settings/project), found in
PostHog under Settings > Project > General
- An optional host URL. Defaults to US Cloud (`https://us.i.posthog.com`). Use
`https://eu.i.posthog.com` for EU Cloud, or your self-hosted URL. The endpoint
path is added automatically.
- An optional service name for log attribution via the OTLP `service.name`
resource attribute. Defaults to your deployment name.

Logs are sent to PostHog using the
[OpenTelemetry (OTLP)](https://posthog.com/docs/logs) log ingestion format. Each
log event includes deployment metadata as resource attributes and the full event
data as the log record body.

### Webhook [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#webhook "Direct link to Webhook")

A webhook log stream is the simplest and most generic stream, allowing piping
logs via POST requests to any URL you configure. The only parameter required to
set up this stream is the desired webhook URL.

A request to this webhook contains as its body a JSON array of events in the
schema defined below.

## Securing webhook log streams [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#securing-webhook-log-streams "Direct link to Securing webhook log streams")

Webhook log stream requests include a signature so you can verify that a request
is legitimate. The request body is signed using HMAC-SHA256 and encoded as a
lowercase hex string, and the resulting signature is included in the
`x-webhook-signature` HTTP header. The HMAC secret is visible in the dashboard
upon configuring the webhook.

To verify the authenticity of a request, sign and encode the request body using
the HMAC secret and
[compare the result in constant time](https://www.chosenplaintext.ca/articles/beginners-guide-constant-time-cryptography.html)
(for instance using
[`SubtleCrypto.verify()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/verify)
in JavaScript) with the signature included in the request header. Note that the
signature is prefixed with `sha256=`.

For additional security, consider validating that the `timestamp` field of the
log event body falls within an acceptable time range to prevent replay attacks.

```typescript
import { Hono } from "hono";

import { env } from "./_generated/server";

const app = new Hono();

app.post("/webhook", async (c) => {

  const payload = await c.req.json();

  const log = payload[0];

  // If using JSONL, parse the first line:

  // const payload = await c.req.text();

  // const log = JSON.parse(payload.split("\n")[0]);

  // Validate that the timestamp of the first log is within 5 minutes

  if (log.timestamp < Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000) {

    c.status(403);

    return c.text("Request expired");

  }

  const signature = c.req.header("x-webhook-signature");

  if (!signature) {

    c.status(401);

    return c.text("Unauthorized");

  }

  const hmacSecret = await crypto.subtle.importKey(

    "raw",

    new TextEncoder().encode(env.WEBHOOK_SECRET),

    { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" },

    false,

    ["verify"],

  );

  const hashPayload = await c.req.arrayBuffer();

  // Use constant-time comparison to verify the payload

  const isValid = await crypto.subtle.verify(

    "HMAC",

    hmacSecret,

    Uint8Array.fromHex(signature.replace("sha256=", "")),

    hashPayload,

  );

  if (isValid) {

    return c.text("Success");

  }

  c.status(401);

  return c.text("Unauthorized");

});

export default app;
```

## Log event schema [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#log-event-schema "Direct link to Log event schema")

info

Log streams configured before May 23, 2024 will use the legacy format
documented on [this\\
page](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams/legacy-event-schema). We
recommend updating your log stream to use the new format.

Log events have a well-defined JSON schema that allow building complex,
type-safe pipelines ingesting log events.

All events will have the following three fields:

- `topic`: string, categorizes a log event, one of
`["verification", "console", "function_execution", "audit_log", "concurrency_stats", "scheduler_stats", "current_storage_usage", "storage_api_bandwidth", "ai_gateway_usage"]`
- `timestamp`: number, Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds as an integer
- `convex`: An object containing metadata related to your Convex deployment,
including `deployment_name`, `deployment_type`, `project_name`, and
`project_slug`.

Note: In the Axiom integration, event-specific information will be available
under the `data` field.

### `verification` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#verification-events "Direct link to verification-events")

This is an event sent to confirm the log stream is working. Schema:

- `topic`: `"verification"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `message`: string

### `console` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#console-events "Direct link to console-events")

Convex function logs via the [`console` API](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/debugging).

Schema:

- `topic`: `"console"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `function`: object, see
[function fields](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams/#function-fields)
- `log_level`: string, one of `["DEBUG", "INFO", "LOG", "WARN", "ERROR"]`
- `message`: string, the
[`object-inspect`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/object-inspect)
representation of the `console.log` payload
- `is_truncated`: boolean, whether this message was truncated to fit within our
logging limits
- `system_code`: optional string, present for automatically added warnings when
functions are approaching [limits](https://docs.convex.dev/production/state/limits#functions)

Example event for `console.log("Sent message!")` from a mutation:

```json
{

    "topic": "console"

    "timestamp": 1715879172882,

    "function": {

      "path": "messages:send",

      "request_id": "d064ef901f7ec0b7",

      "type": "mutation"

    },

    "log_level": "LOG",

    "message": "'Sent message!'"

}
```

### `function_execution` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#function_execution-events "Direct link to function_execution-events")

These events occur whenever a function is run.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"function_execution"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `function`: object, see
[function fields](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams/#function-fields)
- `execution_time_ms`: number, the time in milliseconds this function took to
execute
- `user_execution_time_ms`: optional number, the time in milliseconds the user's
code spent executing (excludes system overhead)
- `status`: string, one of `["success", "failure"]`
- `error_message`: string, present for functions with status `failure`,
containing the error and any stack trace.
- `mutation_queue_length`: optional number (for mutations only), the length of
the per-session mutation queue at the time the mutation was executed. This is
useful for monitoring and debugging mutation queue backlogs in individual
sessions.
- `mutation_retry_count`: number, the number of previous failed executions (for
mutations only) run before a successful one. Only applicable to mutations and
actions.
- `occ_info`: object, if the function call resulted in an OCC (write conflict
between two functions), this field will be present and contain information
relating to the OCC.
[Learn more about write conflicts](https://docs.convex.dev/error/#1).
  - `table_name`: table the conflict occurred in
  - `document_id`: Id of the document that received conflicting writes
  - `write_source`: name of the function that conflicted writes against
    `table_name`
  - `retry_count`: the number of previously failed attempts before the current
    function execution
- `scheduler_info`: object, if set, indicates that the function was originally
invoked by the [scheduler](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions).
  - `job_id`: the job within the
    [`_scheduled_functions`](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions#retrieving-scheduled-function-status)
    table
- `run_reason`: string, why this function ran. One of:
  - `"initialSubscription"`: the first run of a query a client subscribed to
    over the WebSocket sync protocol.
  - `"dataChange"`: a rerun of a query whose subscription was invalidated by a
    write.
  - `"identityChange"`: a rerun of a query caused by the client's auth identity
    changing.
  - `"webSocket"`: a mutation or action called by a client over the WebSocket
    sync protocol.
  - `"httpApi"`: called over the HTTP API, e.g. by `ConvexHttpClient`.
  - `"httpEndpoint"`: an [HTTP action](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/http-actions) serving an
    incoming request to a route in `http.ts`.
  - `"cron"`: called by a [cron job](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/cron-jobs).
  - `"scheduler"`: called by the
    [scheduler](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions).
  - `"action"`: called from another function via `ctx.runQuery`,
    `ctx.runMutation`, or `ctx.runAction`.
  - `"tester"`: a one-off query run via the dashboard's
    [custom query](https://docs.convex.dev/dashboard/deployments/data#writing-custom-queries)
    tester or `npx convex run --inline-query`.
- `usage`:
  - `database_io_read_bytes`: number
  - `database_io_write_bytes`: number, this and `database_io_read_bytes` make up
    the Database I/O used by the function
  - `database_read_documents`: number, the number of documents read by the
    function
  - `database_write_documents`: number, the number of documents inserted,
    updated, or deleted by the function
  - `database_write_index_rows`: number, the number of index entries written by
    the documents counted in `database_write_documents`. Each document write
    costs one entry per database index on its table, counting the built-in
    `by_id` and `by_creation_time` indexes, and changing an indexed field costs
    a second entry to remove the stale one
  - `text_search_query_bytes`: number
  - `text_search_write_query_bytes`: number, these two fields together track
    text search query usage
  - `vector_search_query_bytes`: number
  - `vector_search_write_query_bytes`: number, these two fields together track
    vector search query usage. Combined with the `text_search_*` fields, they
    make up the Search queries pricing metric.
  - `file_storage_read_bytes`: number, the bytes read from file storage using
    the [storage API within Convex functions](https://docs.convex.dev/file-storage/store-files)
    (e.g. `ctx.storage.get()`). This does not include bandwidth from clients
    downloading files directly from the storage HTTP API; see
    [`storage_api_bandwidth`](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams#storage_api_bandwidth-events).
  - `network_egress_bytes`: number, the bytes sent to clients or external
    services. This contributes to Data egress alongside
    [`storage_api_bandwidth`](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams#storage_api_bandwidth-events) events.
  - `audit_log_egress_bytes`: number, the bytes egressed delivering
    [audit logs](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/audit-logging) to S3 (if
    configured for a D1024 deployment).
  - `action_memory_used_mb`: optional number (actions and HTTP actions only),
    the memory used in MiB. This combined with `execution_time_ms` makes up
    Action compute.
  - `function_args_bytes`: optional number, the size of the arguments the
    function was called with. Absent for HTTP actions.
  - `function_returns_bytes`: optional number, the size of the value the
    function returned. Absent for HTTP actions and for failed executions.

Example event for a query:

```json
{

  "data": {

    "execution_time_ms": 294,

    "function": {

      "cached": false,

      "path": "message:list",

      "request_id": "892104e63bd39d9a",

      "type": "query"

    },

    "status": "success",

    "run_reason": "initialSubscription",

    "timestamp": 1715973841548,

    "topic": "function_execution",

    "usage": {

      "database_io_read_bytes": 1077,

      "database_io_write_bytes": 0,

      "database_read_documents": 3,

      "database_write_documents": 0,

      "database_write_index_rows": 0,

      "file_storage_read_bytes": 0,

      "text_search_query_bytes": 0,

      "text_search_write_query_bytes": 0,

      "vector_search_query_bytes": 0,

      "vector_search_write_query_bytes": 0,

      "network_egress_bytes": 0,

      "audit_log_egress_bytes": 0,

      "function_args_bytes": 12,

      "function_returns_bytes": 843

    }

  }

}
```

### `ai_gateway_usage` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#ai_gateway_usage-events "Direct link to ai_gateway_usage-events")

These events report terminal usage for an inference made through the
[AI Gateway](https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/overview). They are emitted after the provider
response has been consumed, which can be later than the related
`function_execution` event.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"ai_gateway_usage"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds when the inference ended
- `function`: optional object containing trusted function attribution:
  - `request_id`: optional string matching the related `function_execution`
    event's `function.request_id`
  - `component_path`: optional string identifying a component
  - `path`: optional string identifying the action or HTTP action
  - `type`: optional string, one of `["action", "http_action"]`
- `inference_id`: string that uniquely identifies the inference. Use this field
to deduplicate events when processing retries.
- `provider`: string naming the provider that reported the usage
- `endpoint`: string, one of
`["chat_completions", "decisions", "embeddings", "images", "messages", "responses", "videos"]`
- `upstream_id`: optional provider request identifier
- `model`: optional provider model identifier
- `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`: optional token counts
- `cached_prompt_tokens`: optional number of prompt tokens served from a cache
- `reasoning_tokens`: optional number of reasoning tokens
- `cost`: number or `null`. This is the provider-reported charge in USD. A value
of `0` is a reported free inference. This value is not an invoice total.
- `cost_unit`: `"USD"`
- `outcome`: string, one of
`["completed", "no_usage", "provider_error", "upstream_error", "abandoned", "oversized"]`
- `environment`: string, one of `["production", "staging"]`

Example event:

```json
{

  "topic": "ai_gateway_usage",

  "timestamp": 1756400000123,

  "function": {

    "request_id": "892104e63bd39d9a",

    "component_path": "agent",

    "path": "chat.js:reply",

    "type": "action"

  },

  "inference_id": "inf_01J7EXAMPLE",

  "provider": "openRouter",

  "endpoint": "messages",

  "upstream_id": "gen-abc123",

  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5",

  "prompt_tokens": 120,

  "completion_tokens": 48,

  "total_tokens": 168,

  "cached_prompt_tokens": 80,

  "reasoning_tokens": 12,

  "cost": 0.0024,

  "cost_unit": "USD",

  "outcome": "completed",

  "environment": "production"

}
```

Delivery uses the existing log-stream guarantees: events may be delayed,
dropped, or duplicated. Deduplicate by deployment and `inference_id` before
summing cost, and count unresolved records separately. In Axiom, the topic
payload is nested under `data`, so the cost field is `data.cost`. Events contain
usage metadata; prompts and model responses are excluded.

### Function fields [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#function-fields "Direct link to Function fields")

The following fields are added under `function` for all `console` and
`function_execution` events:

- `type`: string, one of `["query", "mutation", "action", "http_action"]`
- `path`: string, e.g. `"myDir/myFile:myFunction"`, or `"POST /my_endpoint"`
- `cached`: optional boolean, for queries this denotes whether this event came
from a cached function execution
- `request_id`: string, the
[request ID](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/debugging#finding-relevant-logs-by-request-id) of
the function.

### `concurrency_stats` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#concurrency_stats-events "Direct link to concurrency_stats-events")

These events are sent once a minute, reporting function concurrency statistics.
Events are only sent if the stats have changed. Missing data points should be
interpolated from the previous data event.

Schema:

Each event contains concurrency statistics for each function type (e.g. queries,
mutations, actions). The records for each events have the following schema:

- `num_running`: The maximum number of concurrently running functions within the
minute the metric was reported

- `num_queued`: The maximum number of queued functions within the minute the
metric was reported. Functions may become temporarily queued when concurrency
limits have been reached.

- `topic`: `"concurrency_stats"`

- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds

- `query`: Concurrency stats for queries

- `mutation`: Concurrency stats for mutations

- `action`: Concurrency stats for actions

- `node_action`: Concurrency stats for node actions

- `http_action`: Concurrency stats for HTTP actions


### `scheduler_stats` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#scheduler_stats-events "Direct link to scheduler_stats-events")

These events are periodically sent by the scheduler reporting statistics from
the scheduled function executor.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"scheduler_stats"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `lag_seconds`: The difference between `timestamp` and the scheduled run time
of the oldest overdue scheduled job, in seconds.
- `num_running_jobs`: number, the number of scheduled jobs currently running

### `current_storage_usage` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#current_storage_usage-events "Direct link to current_storage_usage-events")

These events are periodically sent with snapshots of the current storage usage
across your deployment. They provide aggregated totals for all storage types.

These events are not currently sent for self-hosted deployments.

For calculating billing costs:

- Database Storage Bytes: `total_document_size_bytes + total_index_size_bytes`
- File Storage: `total_file_storage_bytes + total_backup_storage_bytes`
- Search Storage: `total_vector_storage_bytes + total_text_storage_bytes`

Schema:

- `topic`: `"current_storage_usage"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `total_document_size_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of all documents
stored in database tables
- `total_index_size_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of all database indexes
- `total_vector_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of vector index
storage
- `total_text_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of text index storage
- `total_file_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of file storage
- `total_backup_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of snapshot/backup
storage
- `total_system_table_document_size_bytes`: object, document size in bytes per
system virtual table (e.g. `_storage`, `_scheduled_functions`)

Example event:

```json
{

  "topic": "current_storage_usage",

  "timestamp": 1715973841548,

  "total_document_size_bytes": 104857600,

  "total_index_size_bytes": 10485760,

  "total_vector_storage_bytes": 5242880,

  "total_text_storage_bytes": 1048576,

  "total_file_storage_bytes": 52428800,

  "total_backup_storage_bytes": 209715200,

  "total_system_table_document_size_bytes": {

    "_storage": 1048576,

    "_scheduled_functions": 2097152

  }

}
```

### `storage_api_bandwidth` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#storage_api_bandwidth-events "Direct link to storage_api_bandwidth-events")

These events are emitted whenever a client downloads a file directly from the
storage HTTP API (`GET /api/storage/*`), for example when using a
[file URL](https://docs.convex.dev/file-storage/serve-files) obtained from `ctx.storage.getUrl()`.
Each HTTP request that serves file bytes produces one event after the download
stream completes or is dropped. This is separate from the
`file_storage_read_bytes` and `file_storage_write_bytes` fields in
[`function_execution`](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams#function_execution-events) events, which track file
bandwidth consumed within Convex functions themselves.

The `egress_bytes` field reports the total bytes actually delivered to the
client, not necessarily the full file size. There are several cases where these
values differ:

- **Range requests**: When a client requests a specific byte range (e.g.
`Range: bytes=0-1023`), only the bytes in that range are reported.
- **Partial downloads**: If a download is abandoned mid-stream (e.g. the user
navigates away), the event reports only the bytes that were delivered before
the connection closed.
- **Browser prefetch behavior**: Browsers may issue multiple requests for the
same file. For example, a browser loading a video may first send a small range
request to read metadata, then follow up with a full request. Each request
produces a separate event, so you may see multiple events with different
`egress_bytes` values for what appears to be a single user download.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"storage_api_bandwidth"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `storage_id`: string, the [document ID](https://docs.convex.dev/database/document-ids) of the
file in the `_storage` system table
- `egress_bytes`: number, the total bytes delivered to the client

Example event:

```json
{

  "topic": "storage_api_bandwidth",

  "timestamp": 1715973841548,

  "storage_id": "k12345678901234567890123456789012",

  "egress_bytes": 1048576

}
```

### `audit_log` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#audit_log-events "Direct link to audit_log-events")

These events represent changes to your deployment, which also show up in the
[History tab](https://dashboard.convex.dev/deployment/history) in the dashboard.

Schema:

- `topic`: `audit_log`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `audit_log_action`: string, e.g. `"create_environment_variable"`,
`"push_config"`, `"change_deployment_state"`
- `audit_log_metadata`: string, stringified JSON holding metadata about the
event. The exact format of this event may change.

Example `push_config` audit log:

```json
{

  "topic": "audit_log",

  "timestamp": 1714421999886,

  "audit_log_action": "push_config",

  "audit_log_metadata": "{\"auth\":{\"added\":[],\"removed\":[]},\"crons\":{\"added\":[],\"deleted\":[],\"updated\":[]},..."

}
```

## Guarantees [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#guarantees "Direct link to Guarantees")

Log events provide a best-effort delivery guarantee. Log streams are buffered
in-memory and sent out in batches to your deployment's configured streams. This
means that logs can be dropped if ingestion throughput is too high. Similarly,
due to network retries, it is possible for a log event to be duplicated in a log
stream.

That's it! Your logs are now configured to stream out. If there is a log
streaming destination that you would like to see supported,
[please let us know](https://docs.convex.dev/production/contact)!

On this page

> For AI agents: see [llms.txt](https://docs.convex.dev/llms.txt) for the complete documentation index. Markdown versions are available by adding .md to a page URL or requesting Accept: text/markdown.

Log streams enable streaming of events such as function executions and
`console.log`s from your Convex deployment to supported destinations, such as
Axiom, Datadog, PostHog, or a custom webhook.

The most recent logs produced by your Convex deployment can be viewed in the
Dashboard [Logs page](https://docs.convex.dev/dashboard/deployments/logs), the
[Convex CLI](https://docs.convex.dev/cli/overview), or in the browser console, providing a quick
and easy way to view recent logs.

Log streaming to a third-party destination like Axiom, Datadog, or PostHog
enables storing historical logs, more powerful querying and data visualization,
and integrations with other tools (e.g. PagerDuty, Slack).

Log streams require a Convex Pro plan.

## Configuring log streams [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#configuring-log-streams "Direct link to Configuring log streams")

We currently support the following log streams, with plans to support many more:

- [Axiom](https://www.axiom.co/)
- [Datadog](https://www.datadoghq.com/)
- [PostHog](https://posthog.com/)
- Webhook to a custom URL

See the instructions for
[configuring an integration](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/#configuring-an-integration).
The specific information needed for each log stream is covered below.

### Axiom [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#axiom "Direct link to Axiom")

Configuring an Axiom log stream requires specifying:

- The name of your
[Axiom dataset](https://axiom.co/docs/reference/settings#dataset)
- An Axiom [API key](https://axiom.co/docs/reference/settings#api-token)
- An optional list of attributes and their values to be included in all log
events send to Axiom. These will be sent via the `attributes` field in the
[Ingest API](https://axiom.co/docs/send-data/ingest#ingest-api).

When configuring a Convex dataset in Axiom, a dashboard will automatically be
created in Axiom. You can find it in the _Integrations_ section of the
_Dashboards_ tab. To customize the layout of the dashboard, you can
[fork it](https://axiom.co/docs/dashboards/create#fork-dashboards).

![A dashboard in Axiom](https://docs.convex.dev/assets/images/axiom_dashboard-a989f50d9d1fe5d65e33ecafb7facea1.png)

### Datadog [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#datadog "Direct link to Datadog")

Configuring a Datadog log stream requires specifying:

- The [site location](https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/site/) of your
Datadog deployment
- A Datadog
[API key](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/api-app-keys/#add-an-api-key-or-client-token)
- A comma-separated list of tags that will be passed using the
[`ddtags` field](https://docs.datadoghq.com/getting_started/tagging/) in all
payloads sent to Datadog. This can be used to include any other metadata that
can be useful for querying or categorizing your Convex logs ingested by your
Datadog deployment.

### PostHog [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#posthog "Direct link to PostHog")

Configuring a PostHog log stream requires specifying:

- A PostHog [project token](https://us.posthog.com/settings/project), found in
PostHog under Settings > Project > General
- An optional host URL. Defaults to US Cloud (`https://us.i.posthog.com`). Use
`https://eu.i.posthog.com` for EU Cloud, or your self-hosted URL. The endpoint
path is added automatically.
- An optional service name for log attribution via the OTLP `service.name`
resource attribute. Defaults to your deployment name.

Logs are sent to PostHog using the
[OpenTelemetry (OTLP)](https://posthog.com/docs/logs) log ingestion format. Each
log event includes deployment metadata as resource attributes and the full event
data as the log record body.

### Webhook [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#webhook "Direct link to Webhook")

A webhook log stream is the simplest and most generic stream, allowing piping
logs via POST requests to any URL you configure. The only parameter required to
set up this stream is the desired webhook URL.

A request to this webhook contains as its body a JSON array of events in the
schema defined below.

## Securing webhook log streams [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#securing-webhook-log-streams "Direct link to Securing webhook log streams")

Webhook log stream requests include a signature so you can verify that a request
is legitimate. The request body is signed using HMAC-SHA256 and encoded as a
lowercase hex string, and the resulting signature is included in the
`x-webhook-signature` HTTP header. The HMAC secret is visible in the dashboard
upon configuring the webhook.

To verify the authenticity of a request, sign and encode the request body using
the HMAC secret and
[compare the result in constant time](https://www.chosenplaintext.ca/articles/beginners-guide-constant-time-cryptography.html)
(for instance using
[`SubtleCrypto.verify()`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/SubtleCrypto/verify)
in JavaScript) with the signature included in the request header. Note that the
signature is prefixed with `sha256=`.

For additional security, consider validating that the `timestamp` field of the
log event body falls within an acceptable time range to prevent replay attacks.

```typescript
import { Hono } from "hono";

import { env } from "./_generated/server";

const app = new Hono();

app.post("/webhook", async (c) => {

  const payload = await c.req.json();

  const log = payload[0];

  // If using JSONL, parse the first line:

  // const payload = await c.req.text();

  // const log = JSON.parse(payload.split("\n")[0]);

  // Validate that the timestamp of the first log is within 5 minutes

  if (log.timestamp < Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000) {

    c.status(403);

    return c.text("Request expired");

  }

  const signature = c.req.header("x-webhook-signature");

  if (!signature) {

    c.status(401);

    return c.text("Unauthorized");

  }

  const hmacSecret = await crypto.subtle.importKey(

    "raw",

    new TextEncoder().encode(env.WEBHOOK_SECRET),

    { name: "HMAC", hash: "SHA-256" },

    false,

    ["verify"],

  );

  const hashPayload = await c.req.arrayBuffer();

  // Use constant-time comparison to verify the payload

  const isValid = await crypto.subtle.verify(

    "HMAC",

    hmacSecret,

    Uint8Array.fromHex(signature.replace("sha256=", "")),

    hashPayload,

  );

  if (isValid) {

    return c.text("Success");

  }

  c.status(401);

  return c.text("Unauthorized");

});

export default app;
```

## Log event schema [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#log-event-schema "Direct link to Log event schema")

info

Log streams configured before May 23, 2024 will use the legacy format
documented on [this\\
page](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams/legacy-event-schema). We
recommend updating your log stream to use the new format.

Log events have a well-defined JSON schema that allow building complex,
type-safe pipelines ingesting log events.

All events will have the following three fields:

- `topic`: string, categorizes a log event, one of
`["verification", "console", "function_execution", "audit_log", "concurrency_stats", "scheduler_stats", "current_storage_usage", "storage_api_bandwidth", "ai_gateway_usage"]`
- `timestamp`: number, Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds as an integer
- `convex`: An object containing metadata related to your Convex deployment,
including `deployment_name`, `deployment_type`, `project_name`, and
`project_slug`.

Note: In the Axiom integration, event-specific information will be available
under the `data` field.

### `verification` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#verification-events "Direct link to verification-events")

This is an event sent to confirm the log stream is working. Schema:

- `topic`: `"verification"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `message`: string

### `console` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#console-events "Direct link to console-events")

Convex function logs via the [`console` API](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/debugging).

Schema:

- `topic`: `"console"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `function`: object, see
[function fields](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams/#function-fields)
- `log_level`: string, one of `["DEBUG", "INFO", "LOG", "WARN", "ERROR"]`
- `message`: string, the
[`object-inspect`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/object-inspect)
representation of the `console.log` payload
- `is_truncated`: boolean, whether this message was truncated to fit within our
logging limits
- `system_code`: optional string, present for automatically added warnings when
functions are approaching [limits](https://docs.convex.dev/production/state/limits#functions)

Example event for `console.log("Sent message!")` from a mutation:

```json
{

    "topic": "console"

    "timestamp": 1715879172882,

    "function": {

      "path": "messages:send",

      "request_id": "d064ef901f7ec0b7",

      "type": "mutation"

    },

    "log_level": "LOG",

    "message": "'Sent message!'"

}
```

### `function_execution` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#function_execution-events "Direct link to function_execution-events")

These events occur whenever a function is run.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"function_execution"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `function`: object, see
[function fields](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams/#function-fields)
- `execution_time_ms`: number, the time in milliseconds this function took to
execute
- `user_execution_time_ms`: optional number, the time in milliseconds the user's
code spent executing (excludes system overhead)
- `status`: string, one of `["success", "failure"]`
- `error_message`: string, present for functions with status `failure`,
containing the error and any stack trace.
- `mutation_queue_length`: optional number (for mutations only), the length of
the per-session mutation queue at the time the mutation was executed. This is
useful for monitoring and debugging mutation queue backlogs in individual
sessions.
- `mutation_retry_count`: number, the number of previous failed executions (for
mutations only) run before a successful one. Only applicable to mutations and
actions.
- `occ_info`: object, if the function call resulted in an OCC (write conflict
between two functions), this field will be present and contain information
relating to the OCC.
[Learn more about write conflicts](https://docs.convex.dev/error/#1).
  - `table_name`: table the conflict occurred in
  - `document_id`: Id of the document that received conflicting writes
  - `write_source`: name of the function that conflicted writes against
    `table_name`
  - `retry_count`: the number of previously failed attempts before the current
    function execution
- `scheduler_info`: object, if set, indicates that the function was originally
invoked by the [scheduler](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions).
  - `job_id`: the job within the
    [`_scheduled_functions`](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions#retrieving-scheduled-function-status)
    table
- `run_reason`: string, why this function ran. One of:
  - `"initialSubscription"`: the first run of a query a client subscribed to
    over the WebSocket sync protocol.
  - `"dataChange"`: a rerun of a query whose subscription was invalidated by a
    write.
  - `"identityChange"`: a rerun of a query caused by the client's auth identity
    changing.
  - `"webSocket"`: a mutation or action called by a client over the WebSocket
    sync protocol.
  - `"httpApi"`: called over the HTTP API, e.g. by `ConvexHttpClient`.
  - `"httpEndpoint"`: an [HTTP action](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/http-actions) serving an
    incoming request to a route in `http.ts`.
  - `"cron"`: called by a [cron job](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/cron-jobs).
  - `"scheduler"`: called by the
    [scheduler](https://docs.convex.dev/scheduling/scheduled-functions).
  - `"action"`: called from another function via `ctx.runQuery`,
    `ctx.runMutation`, or `ctx.runAction`.
  - `"tester"`: a one-off query run via the dashboard's
    [custom query](https://docs.convex.dev/dashboard/deployments/data#writing-custom-queries)
    tester or `npx convex run --inline-query`.
- `usage`:
  - `database_io_read_bytes`: number
  - `database_io_write_bytes`: number, this and `database_io_read_bytes` make up
    the Database I/O used by the function
  - `database_read_documents`: number, the number of documents read by the
    function
  - `database_write_documents`: number, the number of documents inserted,
    updated, or deleted by the function
  - `database_write_index_rows`: number, the number of index entries written by
    the documents counted in `database_write_documents`. Each document write
    costs one entry per database index on its table, counting the built-in
    `by_id` and `by_creation_time` indexes, and changing an indexed field costs
    a second entry to remove the stale one
  - `text_search_query_bytes`: number
  - `text_search_write_query_bytes`: number, these two fields together track
    text search query usage
  - `vector_search_query_bytes`: number
  - `vector_search_write_query_bytes`: number, these two fields together track
    vector search query usage. Combined with the `text_search_*` fields, they
    make up the Search queries pricing metric.
  - `file_storage_read_bytes`: number, the bytes read from file storage using
    the [storage API within Convex functions](https://docs.convex.dev/file-storage/store-files)
    (e.g. `ctx.storage.get()`). This does not include bandwidth from clients
    downloading files directly from the storage HTTP API; see
    [`storage_api_bandwidth`](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams#storage_api_bandwidth-events).
  - `network_egress_bytes`: number, the bytes sent to clients or external
    services. This contributes to Data egress alongside
    [`storage_api_bandwidth`](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams#storage_api_bandwidth-events) events.
  - `audit_log_egress_bytes`: number, the bytes egressed delivering
    [audit logs](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/audit-logging) to S3 (if
    configured for a D1024 deployment).
  - `action_memory_used_mb`: optional number (actions and HTTP actions only),
    the memory used in MiB. This combined with `execution_time_ms` makes up
    Action compute.
  - `function_args_bytes`: optional number, the size of the arguments the
    function was called with. Absent for HTTP actions.
  - `function_returns_bytes`: optional number, the size of the value the
    function returned. Absent for HTTP actions and for failed executions.

Example event for a query:

```json
{

  "data": {

    "execution_time_ms": 294,

    "function": {

      "cached": false,

      "path": "message:list",

      "request_id": "892104e63bd39d9a",

      "type": "query"

    },

    "status": "success",

    "run_reason": "initialSubscription",

    "timestamp": 1715973841548,

    "topic": "function_execution",

    "usage": {

      "database_io_read_bytes": 1077,

      "database_io_write_bytes": 0,

      "database_read_documents": 3,

      "database_write_documents": 0,

      "database_write_index_rows": 0,

      "file_storage_read_bytes": 0,

      "text_search_query_bytes": 0,

      "text_search_write_query_bytes": 0,

      "vector_search_query_bytes": 0,

      "vector_search_write_query_bytes": 0,

      "network_egress_bytes": 0,

      "audit_log_egress_bytes": 0,

      "function_args_bytes": 12,

      "function_returns_bytes": 843

    }

  }

}
```

### `ai_gateway_usage` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#ai_gateway_usage-events "Direct link to ai_gateway_usage-events")

These events report terminal usage for an inference made through the
[AI Gateway](https://docs.convex.dev/ai-gateway/overview). They are emitted after the provider
response has been consumed, which can be later than the related
`function_execution` event.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"ai_gateway_usage"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds when the inference ended
- `function`: optional object containing trusted function attribution:
  - `request_id`: optional string matching the related `function_execution`
    event's `function.request_id`
  - `component_path`: optional string identifying a component
  - `path`: optional string identifying the action or HTTP action
  - `type`: optional string, one of `["action", "http_action"]`
- `inference_id`: string that uniquely identifies the inference. Use this field
to deduplicate events when processing retries.
- `provider`: string naming the provider that reported the usage
- `endpoint`: string, one of
`["chat_completions", "decisions", "embeddings", "images", "messages", "responses", "videos"]`
- `upstream_id`: optional provider request identifier
- `model`: optional provider model identifier
- `prompt_tokens`, `completion_tokens`, `total_tokens`: optional token counts
- `cached_prompt_tokens`: optional number of prompt tokens served from a cache
- `reasoning_tokens`: optional number of reasoning tokens
- `cost`: number or `null`. This is the provider-reported charge in USD. A value
of `0` is a reported free inference. This value is not an invoice total.
- `cost_unit`: `"USD"`
- `outcome`: string, one of
`["completed", "no_usage", "provider_error", "upstream_error", "abandoned", "oversized"]`
- `environment`: string, one of `["production", "staging"]`

Example event:

```json
{

  "topic": "ai_gateway_usage",

  "timestamp": 1756400000123,

  "function": {

    "request_id": "892104e63bd39d9a",

    "component_path": "agent",

    "path": "chat.js:reply",

    "type": "action"

  },

  "inference_id": "inf_01J7EXAMPLE",

  "provider": "openRouter",

  "endpoint": "messages",

  "upstream_id": "gen-abc123",

  "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.5",

  "prompt_tokens": 120,

  "completion_tokens": 48,

  "total_tokens": 168,

  "cached_prompt_tokens": 80,

  "reasoning_tokens": 12,

  "cost": 0.0024,

  "cost_unit": "USD",

  "outcome": "completed",

  "environment": "production"

}
```

Delivery uses the existing log-stream guarantees: events may be delayed,
dropped, or duplicated. Deduplicate by deployment and `inference_id` before
summing cost, and count unresolved records separately. In Axiom, the topic
payload is nested under `data`, so the cost field is `data.cost`. Events contain
usage metadata; prompts and model responses are excluded.

### Function fields [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#function-fields "Direct link to Function fields")

The following fields are added under `function` for all `console` and
`function_execution` events:

- `type`: string, one of `["query", "mutation", "action", "http_action"]`
- `path`: string, e.g. `"myDir/myFile:myFunction"`, or `"POST /my_endpoint"`
- `cached`: optional boolean, for queries this denotes whether this event came
from a cached function execution
- `request_id`: string, the
[request ID](https://docs.convex.dev/functions/debugging#finding-relevant-logs-by-request-id) of
the function.

### `concurrency_stats` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#concurrency_stats-events "Direct link to concurrency_stats-events")

These events are sent once a minute, reporting function concurrency statistics.
Events are only sent if the stats have changed. Missing data points should be
interpolated from the previous data event.

Schema:

Each event contains concurrency statistics for each function type (e.g. queries,
mutations, actions). The records for each events have the following schema:

- `num_running`: The maximum number of concurrently running functions within the
minute the metric was reported

- `num_queued`: The maximum number of queued functions within the minute the
metric was reported. Functions may become temporarily queued when concurrency
limits have been reached.

- `topic`: `"concurrency_stats"`

- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds

- `query`: Concurrency stats for queries

- `mutation`: Concurrency stats for mutations

- `action`: Concurrency stats for actions

- `node_action`: Concurrency stats for node actions

- `http_action`: Concurrency stats for HTTP actions


### `scheduler_stats` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#scheduler_stats-events "Direct link to scheduler_stats-events")

These events are periodically sent by the scheduler reporting statistics from
the scheduled function executor.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"scheduler_stats"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `lag_seconds`: The difference between `timestamp` and the scheduled run time
of the oldest overdue scheduled job, in seconds.
- `num_running_jobs`: number, the number of scheduled jobs currently running

### `current_storage_usage` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#current_storage_usage-events "Direct link to current_storage_usage-events")

These events are periodically sent with snapshots of the current storage usage
across your deployment. They provide aggregated totals for all storage types.

These events are not currently sent for self-hosted deployments.

For calculating billing costs:

- Database Storage Bytes: `total_document_size_bytes + total_index_size_bytes`
- File Storage: `total_file_storage_bytes + total_backup_storage_bytes`
- Search Storage: `total_vector_storage_bytes + total_text_storage_bytes`

Schema:

- `topic`: `"current_storage_usage"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `total_document_size_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of all documents
stored in database tables
- `total_index_size_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of all database indexes
- `total_vector_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of vector index
storage
- `total_text_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of text index storage
- `total_file_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of file storage
- `total_backup_storage_bytes`: number, total size in bytes of snapshot/backup
storage
- `total_system_table_document_size_bytes`: object, document size in bytes per
system virtual table (e.g. `_storage`, `_scheduled_functions`)

Example event:

```json
{

  "topic": "current_storage_usage",

  "timestamp": 1715973841548,

  "total_document_size_bytes": 104857600,

  "total_index_size_bytes": 10485760,

  "total_vector_storage_bytes": 5242880,

  "total_text_storage_bytes": 1048576,

  "total_file_storage_bytes": 52428800,

  "total_backup_storage_bytes": 209715200,

  "total_system_table_document_size_bytes": {

    "_storage": 1048576,

    "_scheduled_functions": 2097152

  }

}
```

### `storage_api_bandwidth` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#storage_api_bandwidth-events "Direct link to storage_api_bandwidth-events")

These events are emitted whenever a client downloads a file directly from the
storage HTTP API (`GET /api/storage/*`), for example when using a
[file URL](https://docs.convex.dev/file-storage/serve-files) obtained from `ctx.storage.getUrl()`.
Each HTTP request that serves file bytes produces one event after the download
stream completes or is dropped. This is separate from the
`file_storage_read_bytes` and `file_storage_write_bytes` fields in
[`function_execution`](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams#function_execution-events) events, which track file
bandwidth consumed within Convex functions themselves.

The `egress_bytes` field reports the total bytes actually delivered to the
client, not necessarily the full file size. There are several cases where these
values differ:

- **Range requests**: When a client requests a specific byte range (e.g.
`Range: bytes=0-1023`), only the bytes in that range are reported.
- **Partial downloads**: If a download is abandoned mid-stream (e.g. the user
navigates away), the event reports only the bytes that were delivered before
the connection closed.
- **Browser prefetch behavior**: Browsers may issue multiple requests for the
same file. For example, a browser loading a video may first send a small range
request to read metadata, then follow up with a full request. Each request
produces a separate event, so you may see multiple events with different
`egress_bytes` values for what appears to be a single user download.

Schema:

- `topic`: `"storage_api_bandwidth"`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `storage_id`: string, the [document ID](https://docs.convex.dev/database/document-ids) of the
file in the `_storage` system table
- `egress_bytes`: number, the total bytes delivered to the client

Example event:

```json
{

  "topic": "storage_api_bandwidth",

  "timestamp": 1715973841548,

  "storage_id": "k12345678901234567890123456789012",

  "egress_bytes": 1048576

}
```

### `audit_log` events [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#audit_log-events "Direct link to audit_log-events")

These events represent changes to your deployment, which also show up in the
[History tab](https://dashboard.convex.dev/deployment/history) in the dashboard.

Schema:

- `topic`: `audit_log`
- `timestamp`: Unix epoch timestamp in milliseconds
- `audit_log_action`: string, e.g. `"create_environment_variable"`,
`"push_config"`, `"change_deployment_state"`
- `audit_log_metadata`: string, stringified JSON holding metadata about the
event. The exact format of this event may change.

Example `push_config` audit log:

```json
{

  "topic": "audit_log",

  "timestamp": 1714421999886,

  "audit_log_action": "push_config",

  "audit_log_metadata": "{\"auth\":{\"added\":[],\"removed\":[]},\"crons\":{\"added\":[],\"deleted\":[],\"updated\":[]},..."

}
```

## Guarantees [​](https://docs.convex.dev/production/integrations/log-streams\#guarantees "Direct link to Guarantees")

Log events provide a best-effort delivery guarantee. Log streams are buffered
in-memory and sent out in batches to your deployment's configured streams. This
means that logs can be dropped if ingestion throughput is too high. Similarly,
due to network retries, it is possible for a log event to be duplicated in a log
stream.

That's it! Your logs are now configured to stream out. If there is a log
streaming destination that you would like to see supported,
[please let us know](https://docs.convex.dev/production/contact)!

content.text: Getting the dashboard's own numbers into the app (not through the script) is possible, but there's a decision you need to make first:

questions.question: The app can't read logs itself, so each deployment has to send them to the app. Which way should I wire it?

options.label: Log streams webhook (Recommended)
options.description: The official route. Each region's dashboard sends execution logs (execution_time_ms, cached) to a signed HTTP endpoint I add, which saves the server ms onto the row. Needs the Convex Pro plan, plus a one-time step per region: you add the webhook URL in the dashboard and give me its secret.

options.label: Poll the logs API with a cron
options.description: Works on the free plan. A scheduled job in each region reads that deployment's logs from the same internal endpoint the CLI uses, with a deploy key stored as an env var. That endpoint isn't documented, so it could break, and the deploy key has full admin access to the deployment.

content.text:
The latency column now shows the dashboard's own time for each insert, and the script is gone. It still shows "—" everywhere until you connect each region's logs in the Convex dashboard. That's the one part I can't do for you, and it needs the **Convex Pro plan**.

**How it works:** each region sends its logs to a new endpoint in the app, `/api/logs` (in `convex/http.ts`). Convex sends a log line from `items:add` with the new row's id, and a separate event with how long that call took. The endpoint pairs the two and saves the time on the row as `serverMs`. The table and tiles show it a few seconds after the row appears.

**Setup, once per region:**

1. In the Convex dashboard, open the region's deployment, then Settings → Integrations → Log streams → **Webhook**. Use that region's URL:

   | region | webhook URL |
   |---|---|
   | us | `https://ardent-kingfisher-453.convex.site/api/logs` |
   | eu | `https://wooden-ocelot-218.eu-west-1.convex.site/api/logs` |
   | au | `https://insightful-crane-62.ap-southeast-2.convex.site/api/logs` |
   | ca | `https://curious-hyena-917.ca-central-1.convex.site/api/logs` |

2. Copy the secret the dashboard shows and save it on that deployment. For the US:
   ```bash
   npx convex env set LOG_STREAM_SECRET <secret> --deployment dev/us
   ```
   Then the same with `dev/eu`, `dev/au` and `dev/ca` and their own secrets.

**What I tested:**
- All four URLs respond. They report "secret not set" until step 2 is done.
- On the site's deployment, which the app doesn't read, I used a throwaway secret, since removed. A badly signed request was rejected, and the two halves of a fake insert got paired correctly.
- The site still loads from `/`.
- Typecheck and lint pass.

The step that writes the time onto a real row hasn't run end to end yet, because no real logs are coming in. Your first insert after setup will exercise it.

**Worth knowing:**
- **Regions will look almost the same.** Server time is about 20–45 ms everywhere because it leaves out network distance, so the table no longer shows how far away each region is.
- **The big median and the chart still use the browser's timing**, so the region comparison stays visible there. Say if you want those switched too.
- **Every tile will be green.** The colour bands are 300 ms / 600 ms / 1 s, which suits network latency. I can give server times their own bands.
- **Removed:** saving browser-measured latency on rows, the saved/live labels, and `pnpm run server-times`. Older rows still have the unused `latencyMs` field, which can be dropped from the schema after your next Delete all.

Nothing is committed yet.

The app side is ready, but no logs are reaching it. Since 21:26, none of the four regions has received a single log batch from Convex. All four secrets are set, and the only calls the endpoint has ever had were my own test requests. So the log stream itself isn't delivering.

I couldn't check the setup myself: the dashboard in the browser pane is signed out, and I won't sign in for you. In each region's dashboard, under Settings → Integrations → Log streams, please check:

1. **A Webhook stream exists and is enabled.** It needs the Pro plan; on the free plan it can't be saved. If you only ran the `env set` command, no stream was created.
2. **The URL is exactly** `https://<deployment>.convex.site/api/logs`. A `.convex.cloud` URL, or one missing `/api`, never reaches the endpoint. The four URLs are in my previous message.
3. **The secret matches.** It has to be the one shown for that stream, saved on that same deployment. A mismatch would still show up as a failed call in the logs, so it's not the cause right now, but it'll matter once batches arrive.

Two other things to know:
- **Rows inserted before the stream was working stay "—" for good.** The endpoint ignores log events older than 5 minutes, which guards against someone replaying an old batch. Only new inserts get a time.
- **Times arrive a few seconds late.** Convex sends logs in batches, so each row's time fills in shortly after the row appears.

Once a stream is connected, insert a few rows in that region and the times should appear. If they still don't, tell me which region and I'll trace it.

content.text:
I can't fix this from here, and I can't see your stream settings. The deployment API that lists log streams needs a deploy key, which your CLI login isn't. I don't want to create one without asking you.

**Where things stand:**
- **The app side works.** All four `/api/logs` endpoints respond, all four secrets are set, and signed test requests are accepted.
- **Convex has never sent a log batch.** Your inserts at 21:38 ran in every region, but no region's `/api/logs` handler has run since my own test requests at 21:26. Nothing came in, so nothing was rejected either.

That means no log stream is delivering to those URLs. Please open the dashboard for one region, say EU, at Settings → Integrations, and tell me (or send a screenshot of) what the Log streams section shows. The usual causes:

1. **No stream was created.** Setting `LOG_STREAM_SECRET` with `env set` doesn't create one. The Webhook stream has to be added on that page.
2. **No Pro plan.** On the free plan the page shows an upgrade prompt and the stream can't be saved.
3. **Wrong URL.** It must be the `.convex.site` address and end in `/api/logs`, e.g. `https://wooden-ocelot-218.eu-west-1.convex.site/api/logs`. A `.convex.cloud` address, or one without `/api`, sends the logs somewhere else.
4. **Still pending.** A new stream shows a "pending" status until Convex confirms it can reach the URL.

If it turns out you're on the free plan, the logs route won't work at all. Tell me and I'll suggest another way to get server times into the app.

content.text:
No. The log stream feature itself doesn't need deploy keys. They would only let me read each region's stream settings from here to find out what's wrong.

- **Easiest:** open Settings → Integrations for one region and send me a screenshot of the Log streams section. That will most likely show the problem for all four, since you probably set them up the same way.
- **If you'd rather I check through the API:** yes, it's one key per deployment, because deploy keys are tied to a single deployment. You'd generate four, one in each region's Settings. Don't paste them into chat. Put them in a local file like `.env.keys`, add it to `.gitignore`, and I'll read it from there. You can delete the keys in the dashboard afterwards.

I'd start with the screenshot.

content.text:
Rate limits for inserts and network tests are paused in all four regions. To check, I inserted 100 rows in every region at once, which would have hit the limit straight away, and all 400 went through with no errors.

The pause is a switch, not a code removal. I added a `PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS` setting and set it on each region's deployment. While it's set, those two limits are skipped. The limits on creating new users and sessions, and on location logging, stay on.

When you're done testing, turn it back off in each region. No redeploy is needed:
```bash
for r in us eu au ca; do npx convex env remove PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS --deployment dev/$r; done
```

While it's paused, anyone using the hosted site can also insert without limits, so don't leave it on longer than you need.

content.text: The hosted site works from start to finish: one row per region inserted, and each shows its **browser** time (US 427 ms, EU 161 ms, AU 467 ms, CA 250 ms). Committing to the PR branch:

input.command:
git branch --show-current && git add convex/ src/ && git status -s && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
feat: fair per-region timing and server time per row

Timing
- Time each insert by its mutation promise. Convex resolves it only once the
  client's queries include the write, so it measures "until it shows up"
  without scanning the list.
- items.list returns a fixed window of the newest 100 rows (was up to 1000),
  so re-running it after a write costs the same in every region regardless
  of table size. The 1000-row insert cap is gone; the rate limit bounds growth.
- The delete worker removes newest rows first, so the visible rows go first.

Server time
- POST /api/logs receives the Convex webhook log stream (HMAC-verified with
  LOG_STREAM_SECRET), pairs items:add's console line (the row id) with its
  execution_time_ms by request id, and stores it on the row as serverMs.
- App HTTP routes move under /api so static hosting keeps the root.
- The table and tiles show server time once it arrives, else this tab's
  browser-measured time, tagged "server" / "browser".

Testing
- PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS env var skips the per-user insert and network-test limits.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
git log --oneline -3 && git push -q 2>&1 | tail -2; git status -sb | head -1

content.text: Pushed; `.claude/launch.json` stayed out. Now updating the PR title and description to cover both commits:

input.command:
gh pr edit 2 --repo saranatour1/Convex-Regions --title "Host on Convex static hosting; fair per-region timing with server time per row" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Two changes, one commit each.

## 1. Host the frontend on Convex static hosting instead of Cloudflare
Serves the built app from Convex using [`@convex-dev/static-hosting`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@convex-dev/static-hosting) instead of the uncommitted Cloudflare Workers assets setup.

Live: https://harmless-narwhal-958.convex.site

- The `staticHosting` component is registered at `/`, and the app's own HTTP routes move under `/api`.
- `pnpm run deploy:site` pushes the backend and uploads `dist/`.
- The OG and Twitter image tags point at the absolute `convex.site` URL.

## 2. Fair per-region timing, plus server time per row
**Timing**
- Each insert is timed by its mutation promise. Convex resolves it only once the client's queries include the write, so it measures "until it shows up" without depending on the list.
- `items.list` returns a fixed window of the newest 100 rows (it used to return up to 1000). Re-running it after each write now costs the same in every region, whatever the table size. The 1000-row insert cap is gone; the per-user rate limit still bounds growth.
- The delete worker removes the newest rows first, so the rows on screen go first.

**Server time (from the Convex dashboard logs)**
- `POST /api/logs` receives the Convex webhook log stream. It checks the HMAC signature against `LOG_STREAM_SECRET` and drops events older than 5 minutes. It then pairs `items:add`'s console line (the row id) with its `execution_time_ms` by request id, and saves the result on the row as `serverMs`.
- The table and tiles show the server time once it arrives. Until then they show this tab's browser-measured time, tagged `server` or `browser`.

**Testing switch**
- When the `PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS` env var is set, the per-user insert and network-test limits are skipped. The new-user and session limits stay on.

## Setup still needed
- **Log streams (Pro plan):** for each regional deployment, add a Webhook log stream pointing to `https://<deployment>.convex.site/api/logs`, then set its secret with `npx convex env set LOG_STREAM_SECRET <secret> --deployment dev/<region>`. So far no stream has delivered a batch, so every row shows `browser`.
- **Rate limits:** `PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS` is currently **on** in all four regions for testing. Turn it off with `npx convex env remove PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS --deployment dev/<region>`.
- **Old field:** `items.latencyMs` stays in the schema only because existing dev rows still carry it. Drop it after the next "Delete all".

## Testing
- Typecheck and lint pass. Pushed to all four regional dev deployments, and deployed the site to `harmless-narwhal-958`.
- On the hosted site, one insert per region showed browser times of US 427 ms, EU 161 ms, AU 467 ms and CA 250 ms, with no console errors.
- 100 inserts per region went through with `PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS` on.
- The webhook rejects a bad signature (401), and pairs split halves when they arrive as JSON or JSONL. The step that writes a time onto a real row hasn't run end to end, because no log stream is delivering yet.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" && echo UPDATED

content.text:
I deployed the new build to Convex static hosting and added it to PR #2 as a second commit: [saranatour1/Convex-Regions#2](https://github.com/saranatour1/Convex-Regions/pull/2). I also rewrote the PR title and description to cover both commits.

Before committing I went over the whole diff and fixed two things: a bit of formatting noise, and splitting webhook log batches into chunks so a busy one can't exceed Convex's per-mutation limits. Typecheck and lint pass. The code is on all four regional deployments, and on the hosted site one insert per region showed US 427 ms, EU 161 ms, AU 467 ms and CA 250 ms, with no console errors. `.claude/launch.json` was not committed.

### Server time: changed lines
| What | Where |
|---|---|
| `items:add` logs the new row's id so it can be matched to its log entry | [convex/items.ts:36](convex/items.ts:36) |
| New `serverMs` field on rows | [convex/schema.ts:9](convex/schema.ts:9) |
| `list` returns `serverMs` | [convex/items.ts:22](convex/items.ts:22), [convex/items.ts:25](convex/items.ts:25) |
| Webhook endpoint: checks the secret, keeps `execution_time_ms` | [convex/http.ts:13](convex/http.ts:13), [convex/http.ts:16](convex/http.ts:16), [convex/http.ts:45-46](convex/http.ts:45) |
| Matches the id with its time and writes it onto the row | [convex/serverTimes.ts:7](convex/serverTimes.ts:7), [convex/serverTimes.ts:28](convex/serverTimes.ts:28) |
| Secret setting, and app routes moved under `/api` | [convex/convex.config.ts:8-12](convex/convex.config.ts:8) |
| Table: server time if it has arrived, otherwise browser time | [src/components/RowTable.tsx:23-24](src/components/RowTable.tsx:23) |
| Tiles: same fallback | [src/components/TileGrid.tsx:12](src/components/TileGrid.tsx:12), [src/components/TileGrid.tsx:16](src/components/TileGrid.tsx:16) |

### Median time
The median formula didn't change. What changed is how each insert is timed, and that timing is what feeds the median:

| What | Where | Changed? |
|---|---|---|
| Each insert is timed from send until its write resolves | [src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:105-111](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:105) | **yes** |
| Fixed 100-row list in every region, so the timing doesn't depend on table size | [convex/items.ts:11](convex/items.ts:11), [convex/items.ts:24](convex/items.ts:24) | **yes** |
| The run's times are turned into stats at the end of a run | [src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:39-40](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:39) | no |
| Median (p50) calculation | [src/lib/stats.ts:24](src/lib/stats.ts:24) | no |
| Big median number on each region card | [src/components/RegionBlock.tsx:58-61](src/components/RegionBlock.tsx:58) | no |
| "Fastest" region is the lowest median | [src/views/LatencyView.tsx:26](src/views/LatencyView.tsx:26), [src/views/CompareView.tsx:23](src/views/CompareView.tsx:23) | no |

### Still open
- **Server times aren't arriving yet.** No region's log stream has delivered anything, so every row shows `browser`. The step that writes a time onto a real row hasn't run end to end; my test only covered a fake id. Your first insert after the streams are fixed will exercise it.
- **Rate limits are still paused** in all four regions, and that includes the public site. Turn them back on when you're done testing:
  ```bash
  for r in us eu au ca; do npx convex env remove PAUSE_RATE_LIMITS --deployment dev/$r; done
  ```
- **`items.latencyMs` is still in the schema** only because existing rows carry it. Remove it after the next Delete all.

content.text:
The graph works again. It wasn't a data problem: the chart was drawing into a box 0 px tall. Its height was set as a percentage of a parent with no fixed height, which is what happens in a narrow window like yours where the page scrolls. Recharts then had no room and drew nothing. That bug came in with the earlier commit that added the chart, not with this PR's changes.

**Fix (2 lines):** the chart now fills a box that is at least 256 px tall and grows to fill the panel. The changes are in [LatencyChart.tsx:18-21](src/components/LatencyChart.tsx:18) and [CompareView.tsx:74](src/views/CompareView.tsx:74).

**Verified after inserting 50 rows per region:**
| Width | Chart size | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| 519 px (yours) | 461 × 516 | 4, 50 points each |
| 1440 px | 1094 × 649, no page scroll | 4, 50 points each |

Both sizes work on the local dev server and on the hosted site, which I redeployed. A clean page load shows no console errors. The hook-order errors I saw while debugging came from hot reloads during editing, not the app.

**PR:** I pushed the fix as a third commit on `feat/convex-static-hosting` (`c718b6c`) and added it to the PR description. GitHub hasn't caught up yet: the PR still lists 2 commits even though the branch has the new one. It usually updates within a minute or two.

The first push attempt failed because your `origin` still points at the repository's old name, `Demo-Regions`. I pushed to the new URL directly. To stop this happening again:
```bash
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/saranatour1/Convex-Regions.git
```

lastPrompt: where's the change happening, how is the latency recorded?

content.text:
Each row's latency is recorded in one of two ways. The browser always times it, and the Convex logs can add a server time on top.

### 1. Browser time (what you see now, tagged `BROWSER`)
This all happens in your browser, in [src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts):

1. **Start the clock.** Just before sending each insert, it records the time ([line 105](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:105)): `const sentAt = performance.now()`.
2. **Send the insert** to that region with `add(...)` ([line 107](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:107)).
3. **Stop the clock** when the insert's promise resolves ([line 111](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:111)): `const t = now - sentAt`. Convex resolves it only once your browser's live data already includes the new row. So `t` is the full trip: browser → region → saved → back to your screen.
4. **Use the result:**
   - The row's own time is stored by key, and the table and tiles show it ([line 113](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:113)).
   - The chart's point list is updated ([line 114](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:114)).
   - The time is added to the run's list (`r.lat`, [line 112](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:112)).
5. **When the run ends,** that list becomes the median, p95 and total ([lines 39–40](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:39)). The median is calculated in [stats.ts:24](src/lib/stats.ts:24) and shown as the big number on each card in [RegionBlock.tsx:59](src/components/RegionBlock.tsx:59).

These times are never saved. They only exist in the tab that ran the test, so they disappear on reload.

### 2. Server time (tagged `SERVER` — arrives only once log streams work)
This happens on the Convex side:

1. `items:add` logs the new row's id ([convex/items.ts:36](convex/items.ts:36)).
2. Convex sends its logs to `/api/logs`. The endpoint takes the id from the log line and `execution_time_ms` from the matching execution event ([convex/http.ts:44-46](convex/http.ts:44)). These are the same numbers as on the dashboard.
3. The two are matched up, and the time is saved on the row as `serverMs` ([convex/serverTimes.ts:28](convex/serverTimes.ts:28)).

### Which number a row shows
[RowTable.tsx:23](src/components/RowTable.tsx:23) and [TileGrid.tsx:12](src/components/TileGrid.tsx:12) both use `serverMs ?? latency[key]`. A row shows the server time if one has arrived, and the browser time otherwise.

### What keeps it fair between regions
Each region's list query returns the same fixed 100 newest rows ([convex/items.ts:24](convex/items.ts:24)). Re-running it after each insert therefore costs the same in every region, however big its table is.

Deletes are timed differently. The browser watches the list and records the moment each row disappears ([useRegionBench.ts:52-60](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:52)).

input.description: Find all performance.now calls

content.text:
`performance.now()` is only ever called in the browser, never in the Convex functions. It appears in two files:

**[src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts): the Latency and Compare tabs**

| Line | When it runs | What it's for |
|---|---|---|
| [91](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:91) | A run starts | `start` of the whole run, used for "all visible" / "all deleted" |
| [105](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:105) | Just before each insert is sent | `sentAt` for that row |
| [108](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:108) | The insert's promise resolves (the row is now in the browser's data) | `now`; the row's time is `now - sentAt` (line 111) |
| [123](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:123) | An insert was rate-limited | Ends the run if this was the last one outstanding |
| [131](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:131) | Delete all is clicked | Send time, shared by every visible row |
| [56](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:56) | A list update arrives during a delete | `now` for each row that has disappeared |

(Line [21](src/hooks/useRegionBench.ts:21) is only a comment.)

**[src/lib/stats.ts:12-14](src/lib/stats.ts:12): the Network test tab**

The `time()` helper wraps a call: it reads the clock, waits for the call to finish, and returns the difference. [netTest.ts](src/lib/netTest.ts) uses it for each WebSocket ping, HTTP ping, and the 128 B and 4 MB echoes.

`performance.now()` counts in milliseconds, with fractions, from when the page loaded. It doesn't jump when your computer's clock changes, which makes it better than `Date.now()` for timing.

content: what does pct and p50 and p95 even mean

message.content: what does pct and p50 and p95 even mean

content.text:
They're percentiles: different ways to summarise a list of times.

**`pct` is the helper that finds a percentile** ([stats.ts:17-18](src/lib/stats.ts:17)). It sorts the times from fastest to slowest and picks the value a given fraction of the way down the list:

```ts
const pct = (sorted: number[], p: number) =>
  sorted[Math.min(sorted.length - 1, Math.floor(sorted.length * p))];
```

**p50 is the median.** Half the writes were faster than this and half were slower. It's the "typical" time, and it's the big number on each card.

**p95 means 95% of writes were at least this fast.** Only the slowest 5% took longer. It shows how bad the slow cases get without being thrown off by a single outlier.

**Example with 10 inserts**, sorted fastest to slowest:

```
250  270  277  290  352  364  392  438  439  900   (ms)
                         ↑                    ↑
                p50 = index 5 → 364     p95 = index 9 → 900
```

- **p50 = 364 ms**: a typical write.
- **p95 = 900 ms**: one slow write. With only 10 samples, p95 is just the slowest one; with 100 inserts it would ignore the worst 5.
- **max = 900 ms**: the single slowest.
- **total**: time from the start of the run until the last write showed up. That's the "all visible" number on the card.

The median is the headline rather than the average because a single slow write pulls the average up a lot, while the median barely moves.

in my honset opinion,these numbers are effectively wrong as it's calculating the time taken from the request itself, not the time taken to get to the client in time,
